## Overview of findings
### Key takeaways
- Build single-leg control and a strength base
- Add velocity through the lower half: drive, stride and hip rotation

### Strengths
- **Cleared for full activity.** Health assessment 2026-09-12.

### Opportunities for growth
- **Fastball velocity is dropping: 58.6 mph.** Latest session Sep 17 bullpen averaged 58.6 mph vs 59.5 mph across the previous 3 (-0.9 mph); top 59.4 mph. Normal session-to-session variation here is about ±0.3 mph.

- **Box jump: Clearance issues above 20 in.** Weak linear load in pitching. Training: Hip extension training and ground force training.

### Notes

### Root cause: why each finding fired

- **Shoulder PVC: Fail:** Shoulder PVC: fail = needs shoulder mobility exercises, pre and post pitching care. Source: Coach's movement assessment protocol (supplied 2026-10-01).
- **Box jump: Clearance issues above 20 in:** Box jump: clearance issues after 20 in = hip extension training, ground force training. Source: Coach's movement assessment protocol (supplied 2026-10-01).
- **Squat mobility: knee: Knee 70% left:** Squat mobility: 75% or lower in the knee = posterior load training to protect knee health. Source: Coach's movement assessment protocol (supplied 2026-10-01).
- **Single-leg balance 39% different side to side:** Side-to-side gap ≥ 30%

## Pitching program
4-week off-season block, 3 pitching days per week. Pitch counts are ranges for the whole session including warm-up pitches.

### Week 1: Settle in: moderate volume, sharp mechanics
- **Day 1, Drill work (21-30 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.
- **Day 2, Bullpen (34-47 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. About half the pitches at full intent with PitchLogic speed feedback after each pitch; rest 20-30 s between. Mix: Fastball, Changeup, Rise ball.
- **Day 3, Spin and movement (26-34 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Spin drills on each pitch type; note spin rate and direction on PitchLogic.

### Week 2: Build: a little more volume and intent
- **Day 1, Drill work (24-33 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.

## Weight room program
**Main program: Lower-half power and drive.** More force into the ground from the drive and stride legs, and faster hip rotation, which is where most windmill velocity comes from.
- Movement screen (box jump or broad jump): hip extension and ground force training, so Lower-half power.
- 4D Motion data on file: Rotational power added to train pelvis-to-trunk sequencing.
- Arm care is part of every pitcher's week.
- Movement screen (hip, shoulder or squat mobility): Mobility circuit added.

### From the movement screen
Training the coach's protocol prescribes for this athlete's results:
- Shoulder mobility exercises, plus pre- and post-pitching care
- Hip extension training and ground force training
- Posterior load training to protect knee health

### Lower-half power: Day A (Force production)
Warm-up: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 3 x 3 broad jumps.
- Trap bar deadlift: 4 x 5 at RPE 7-8 (Push the floor away)
- Rear-foot elevated split squat: 3 x 6 each at RPE 7-8
- Lateral bound to stick: 3 x 4 each (Land soft, hold 2 s, drive-leg push)
- Copenhagen plank (short lever): 2 x 15-20 s each
- Farmer carry: 3 x 30 m at RPE 7

### Lower-half power: Day B (Speed and hip strength)
Warm-up: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 3 x 10 m sprints.
- Box jump (step down): 4 x 3 (Full intent, quiet landing)
- Kettlebell swing: 3 x 10 at RPE 7
- Lateral lunge: 3 x 8 each at RPE 7
- Side-lying hip external rotation (band or cable): 3 x 12 each (Drive-hip external rotation strength)
- Single-leg glute bridge: 3 x 10 each

Progression: Keep jumps and bounds at low reps with full rest; add load to deadlift and split squat only when every rep is crisp. Deload every fourth week.

### Rotational power: Day A (Rotational power)
Warm-up: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 2 x 5 med ball scoop tosses (light).
- Medicine ball scoop toss (2-3 kg): 4 x 4 each side (Hips lead, arms follow)
- Medicine ball step-behind rotational throw: 3 x 4 each side
- Landmine rotation: 3 x 6 each side at RPE 7
- Goblet squat: 3 x 8 at RPE 7
- Half-kneeling cable chop: 3 x 8 each side

### Rotational power: Day B (Trunk stiffness and upper back)
Warm-up: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10.
- Anti-rotation split-stance cable press: 3 x 8 each side
- Chest-supported dumbbell row: 3 x 10 at RPE 7
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 each at RPE 7
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 25 m each hand
- Side plank with top-leg raise: 2 x 8 each side

Progression: Med ball work stays light and fast; progress by intent and distance, not ball weight. Add strength-lift load 2.5-5% when all reps feel RPE 7 or easier. Deload every fourth week.

### Add-on: Arm care and scapular durability
Arm care (10-15 min, most days).
- Band external rotation at 0° and 90°: 2 x 15 each
- Prone Y-T-W: 2 x 8 each
- Serratus wall slide with lift-off: 2 x 10
- Half-kneeling band row to external rotation: 2 x 10 each
- Eccentric biceps curl (light, slow 4 s lower): 2 x 8 each
- Sleeper or cross-body stretch (only if cleared by the clinician): 2 x 30 s

### Add-on: Hip and thoracic mobility
Mobility circuit (15 min, 3-4 x per week).
- 90/90 hip switch with lift-off: 2 x 6 each side
- Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with reach: 2 x 30 s each
- Quadruped hip rotation (CARs): 2 x 5 each direction
- Open-book thoracic rotation: 2 x 8 each side
- Quadruped thread-the-needle: 2 x 8 each side
- Deep goblet squat hold with pry: 2 x 30 s

### Weekly schedule
- **Week 1** (RPE at the low end of each range): Lower-half power Day A, Lower-half power Day B
- **Week 2** (Progress per the program's rule): Lower-half power Day A, Lower-half power Day B
- **Week 3** (Progress per the program's rule): Lower-half power Day A, Lower-half power Day B
- **Week 4** (Deload: cut sets by a third, keep technique crisp): Lower-half power Day A, Lower-half power Day B

### Cautions
- Schedule Day A at least 48 hours before a hard bullpen.
- Skip jumps and bounds on days with lower-body soreness or pain.
- Stop rotational throws with any low-back pain; replace with anti-rotation holds.
- Any shoulder or elbow pain during arm care: stop and tell the coach.
- Internal-rotation deficits are flagged for the clinician; the stretch is included only with their okay.
- Mobility work should never be painful; stop and tell the coach if it is.
